rounds.text: Ram Info Ltd trades at an exceptionally low price-to-book ratio of 0.50x, offering a substantial discount on its underlying assets compared to the sector benchmark price-to-book of 2.01x [E2, E7]. The company is almost debt free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x, having successfully reduced its borrowings down to Rs 4.27 Cr from Rs 8.30 Cr a year earlier [E37, E39, E51]. Furthermore, recent operating performance shows a massive inflection point, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 131% and a compounded profit growth of 109% [E17, E21]. This sharp operational acceleration has outpaced the stock price over the last year, with fundamentals improving rapidly while sentiment remains lagged [E48, E68]. Finally, the stock trades at an attractive EV/EBITDA of 2.39x, which represents a massive discount relative to the sector benchmark of 11.53x [E11]. Conceded: [E34], [E45], [E59].

Despite a low price-to-book ratio, the fundamental engine of Ram Info Ltd suffers from severe structural weakness, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of -12% [E15] and a 3-year compounded profit growth of -34% [E20]. This top-line erosion is compounded by deeply negative cash generation, with operating cash flow plunging to Rs -16.71 Cr and free cash flow hitting Rs -18.80 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], yielding an alarming cash conversion rate of -9.39x [E34]. Profit quality is further compromised by the inclusion of Rs 2.83 Cr in other income [E58], alongside crippling working capital inefficiencies manifest in exceptionally high debtors of 386 days [E59]. Valuation models expose this optimism, with a discounted cash flow analysis indicating an intrinsic value below the market price and a negative margin of safety of -32.6% [E44, E45], while the stock languishes near its 52-week low at just 6% of its range [E5]. Conceded: the company has reduced debt and trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.50x [E39, E52].
